correctness.rationale: The graph model matches the two-rail, odd-rung H_{1x1xn} of Chandrakar--Singh (arXiv:2512.21318v1, Theorem 3.1), which supplies the two-dimensional single-degree rational homology. For each involution, invariant independent faces are unions of admissible vertex orbits. Orientation parity yields exact reduced Lefschetz trace -I(Q_g;-1), and Hopf trace gives tr(g)=(-1)^(n+1) I(Q_g;-1). Row exchange gives n isolated orbits. The longitudinal reflection gives a smaller original chain if n even and a terminal adjacent-supported leaf pair if n odd. The product gives a terminal leaf pair if n even and a smaller original chain with a triangular cap if n odd (with n=1 explicitly treated). For the adjacent-supported leaf pair, toggling leaves cancels all independent-set weights. All four traces and rational character multiplicities follow without extrapolation. Verified by 56 exact orbit evaluations and 16 independent signed fixed-face enumerations. No integral eigenspace splitting is claimed.

originality.rationale: A new top-homology group character is identified for the canonical two-reflection action on planar hexagonal chains. Chandrakar--Singh prove the non-equivariant homotopy type, which does not imply the action. The closest indexed mathematical findings are on other graph complexes or automorphism actions on finite topological models. Jonsson concerns periodically identified infinite lattices, not the same planar chain. No equivalent stronger claim was found in source statements and targeted searches, subject to residual unindexed and inaccessible-publication risk.
residual_risks: A potentially relevant older periodic-grid paper (Jonsson 2010) could not be excluded by full-text inspection; its accessible abstract concerns different periodic objects, so this is a bounded residual coverage risk, not a decisive unresolved same-object claim.
Unindexed, unpublished, or non-English equivalent treatment of reflection characters might exist.
The proof rests on Chandrakar--Singh Theorem 3.1 as a published external homotopy input; its full all-parameter correctness is not independently reproved here.

value.rationale: The canonical row and end symmetries of an infinite family of hexagon chains act on two n-dimensional homology generators, whose symmetry type is invisible to the established non-equivariant wedge classification. The complete four-character formula and module decomposition give a natural exact equivariant topological invariant, separating parity and residue classes of the chain length. The proof extracts this from a geometric quotient-graph simplification and a local cancellation lemma, not merely from finite data. The object, invariant, and need for the exact traces are intrinsic to the symmetry of the studied planar hexagonal chains. No downstream or general equivariant-homotopy claim is asserted.
